claims.content: System Operator
Any JU may report on a previously reported emergency point through operator action only when that JU has additional or more current information on the point.

missing_aspects: The claim identifies 'System Operator' as the actor, but the source text specifies 'Any JU' (Joint Unit) performs the reporting via operator action.

claims.content: The Emergency Point Report is transmitted as a J3.1 message.
Each reported point is assigned a TN(s) by the reporting JU, and its position is reported using geodetic latitude/longitude values.
The latest JU to report the point has R² for that point.

When the reporting JU assumes R² for the emergency point, the transmitted report uses the same TN Reference and the same value of TN Previously Reported as those reported by the previous reporting unit.
Alerts are not used for the J3.1 Emergency Point message since these points cannot be filtered.
The System Operator has information about an emergency condition that requires search and rescue efforts.
An emergency point has been previously reported, and the System Operator has additional or more current information on that emergency point.
To report the existence of an emergency condition requiring search and rescue efforts by initiating an Emergency Point Report.

scope_contract.goal_statement: To report the existence of an emergency condition requiring search and rescue efforts by initiating an Emergency Point Report.
scope_contract.canonical_success_scenario: The System Operator, acting for a JU, initiates one Emergency Point Report for an emergency point requiring search and rescue; in this instance, the point has been previously reported and the System Operator has additional or more current information to include in the report.
scope_contract.start_boundary: The System Operator has information about an emergency condition requiring search and rescue, including additional or more current information on a previously reported emergency point.
scope_contract.success_boundary: The Emergency Point Report has been initiated by the System Operator.
in_scope_actions: Report the existence of the emergency condition requiring search and rescue
Include additional or more current information on a previously reported emergency point when available
excluded_adjacent_actions: Post-report R² administration or responsibility transfer
Database acceptance and acknowledgement by receiving JUs
Downstream SAR tasking or follow-on reporting
variant_dimensions: Reporting context: initial issuance of an Emergency Point Report vs report on a previously reported emergency point with additional/current information

claims.content: If the System Operator attempts to initiate an Emergency Point Report on a Reference Point or Space/Ballistic Missile Track, the Emergency Point Report shall not be initiated.

It is illegal to change a reference or emergency point to any other type of surveillance entity; i.e., the Reference TN used to identify a particular reference or emergency point shall not be used for any other type of entity reported on the interface except in the normal course of TN reuse.
Alerts are not used for the J3.1 Emergency Point message since these points cannot be filtered.
Force Tell and Emergency Indicators, when set in J3 messages, allow these messages to override all operator controllable data filters.

missing_aspects: Recovery or continuation after an illegal emergency-point type change is not documented in the evidence.
Specific main_flow step-number divergence points are not determinable because the main_flow slot was not provided.
Explicit exit state (e.g., 'terminate') is not defined in the cited evidence.
Explicit system response (e.g., 'rejected') and exit state are not defined in the cited evidence.
The specific exit outcome ('the Emergency Point Report is initiated without applying alerts') is not explicitly stated in the cited evidence.
The application of this rule specifically to the J3.1 Emergency Point Report and the resulting exit state ('message proceeds unfiltered') are not supported by the cited evidence.

claims.content: The System Operator initiates an Emergency Point Report through operator action only to report the existence of an emergency condition requiring search and rescue.
The System Operator includes additional or more current information on a previously reported emergency point in the Emergency Point Report.

The Emergency Point Report contains the assigned TN(s) and geodetic latitude/longitude position for the point; when the reporting JU assumes R² for the emergency point, the report uses the same TN Reference and the same TN Previously Reported value as those reported by the previous reporting unit.
The Emergency Point Report is transmitted as a J3.1 message.
The System Operator initiates the Emergency Point Report to report the existence of an emergency condition requiring search and rescue efforts.
Diverges from Step 4: If the Exercise Indicator is set to value 1 in the J3.1 Emergency Point Report, the report is for exercise purposes and is not an actual emergency.

missing_aspects: Evidence supporting the specific condition distinguishing 'initial issuance' from reports on 'previously reported emergency points' as a trigger for this flow.

quality_flags.detail: [mainflow_postconditions_reachability] The postcondition 'Alerts are not used for the J3.1 Emergency Point message since these points cannot be filtered' is not produced or addressed by any Main Flow step. The Main Flow ends with transmission as a J3.1 message, but it never states or implies that alerting is suppressed or not used for that message. This postcondition relies on evidence card EC-EF-018 that is absent from the Main Flow, creating a vertical gap where the postcondition is an unsupported system constraint rather than a reachable result of the Main Flow.

[exceptionflow_exit_coverage] Exception flow claim 4 states a general J3-message capability (Force Tell and Emergency Indicators allow messages to override operator filters) but does not give the Emergency Point Report branch a clear outcome: it does not return to a main-flow step, terminate/hand off, or end in an explicit terminal failure/prevention state for the J3.1 Emergency Point Report.

inconsistency_hints: Postcondition 5 asserts that all receiving JUs accept the emergency alert in their databases, but the main flow stops at transmitting the J3.1 message and does not include any receiving-JU database acceptance step. The goal scope contract explicitly excludes 'Database acceptance and acknowledgement by receiving JUs' as an adjacent action, so this postcondition lies outside the current use-case boundary and is not reachable from the stated main flow.

Main Flow step 3 only requires the report to contain assigned TN(s) and geodetic latitude/longitude. It does not require the TN Reference / TN Previously Reported continuity with the previous reporting unit that Postcondition 4 makes mandatory when the reporting JU assumes R². Consequently, the J3.1 report transmitted at step 4 is not shown to satisfy that postcondition.
